messages:
izzy: Heads-up  proposing a different take for the console_events schema migration: add a route_fp fingerprint column and use a narrow partial index + backfill pipeline, instead of the wide tenant_shard approach.

izzy: Motivation: we get finer-grained distribution for heavy routes, can keep index bloat minimal with partial indexes, and simplify multi-tenant aggregates.

marcos: sounds interesting. do you have a DDL sketch and how the read path changes?

izzy: DDL sketch (safe, non-blocking parts only):

```
BEGIN;
ALTER TABLE console_events ADD COLUMN route_fp bigint DEFAULT NULL;
-- partial index targets only rows migrated/dual-written to avoid filling index with NULLs
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_console_events_fp_ts ON console_events (route_fp, ts DESC) WHERE route_fp IS NOT NULL;
-- keep legacy PK/index intact for now
COMMIT;
```

izzy: Read planner idea: prefer the fingerprint index when route_fp is present (dual-write phase), otherwise fall back to legacy index. We'll implement a planner function in the query layer that builds a UNION ALL: first query against the fp-indexed slice, second against legacy rows that still have NULL fp. That avoids ORs that block index use.

priya: can you paste the union outline? ORs are expensive so union strategy makes sense.

izzy: sample read pattern:

```
-- n is limit; fetch n from partitioned rows then fill from legacy rows
(SELECT * FROM console_events WHERE route_fp = :fp AND ts < :end ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT :n)
UNION ALL
(SELECT * FROM console_events WHERE route_fp IS NULL AND route_id = :route AND ts < :end ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT :n)
LIMIT :n;
```

jong: good. union keeps both indexes usable. what's the dual-write strategy? writes won't always succeed to new column in early rollouts.

izzy: dual-write plan: API/ingest sets route_fp = fingerprint64(route_id) % fp_mod when the migration flag is ON. We'll default fp_mod=64 but make it per-cluster-configurable. Writes will be idempotent and include request-level migration metadata via headers so we can track partial failures.

tom: backfill approach? full-table updates are scary.

izzy: backfill pipeline: windowed, streaming-friendly job. workers claim route_id ranges from a coordinator queue (Kafka) and do idempotent upserts for rows in a time window. Each worker records progress to `migration_audit` topic. That lets us resume and throttle. We'll run non-overlapping windows to reduce hotspotting.

marcos: how long do we retain legacy rows and is there a compaction plan?

izzy: plan: retain legacy rows for 21 days after a tenant's backfill completes. After that, a safe delete pass removes rows where route_fp IS NOT NULL and legacy duplicates exist. We also plan a daily compaction job that consolidates old rows into rollups for 90+ day retention window.

priya: telemetry / alerts we need: migration.job, migration.window, migration.errors, migration.progress_pct. Also tag traces with migration.phase so Optimize/console can graph regressions against baseline.

ops-bot: migration_streamer started job=fp-backfill-20260304 window=2026-03-01..2026-03-03 workers=8

jong: rollout checklist suggestion: 1) add column + partial index, 2) enable dual-write in staging, 3) run backfill on a copy of prod data and collect perf telemetry, 4) enable read planner in staging, run saved-chart battery, 5) small canary tenants (5), 6) expand canary by traffic percent.

marcos: also add a quick toggle in the query layer to force legacy-only or fp-only paths for fast rollback. Prefer feature-flag driven selector.

izzy: agreed. feature flag + kill-switch endpoint. We'll also record a migration assertion metric that fails if row counts diverge by >0.1% after backfill (configurable).

priya: saved-chart battery: I'll pick 10 high-p99 charts and run them against the backfilled staging db. we'll snapshot token counts and DB CPU.

deploy-bot: fp-backfill job worker-3 reported 8% of rows had null route_id -> skipping. ticket created: #OPS-4821

izzy: thanks. those null route_ids need a fallback fingerprint (use tenant_id or hash of other fields) for correctness. add to backfill transformation.

tom: what about cross-tenant aggregates (org or company view)? union read may be okay but full-cluster aggregates might need a new rollup materialized view keyed by day+org_id.

izzy: yes we'll create `console_events_rollup_fp_v1` and populate from both shapes during migration. rollup parity check will be part of the audit pipeline.

marcos: performance tuning: partial index size is limited only to migrated rows, nice. but we need to monitor index bloat and VACUUMing patterns during heavy backfill. schedule low-IO windows.

priya: add migration.telemetry.phase values: plan, dualwrite, backfill, cutover, cleanup. also emit migration.backfill.batch tags. Optimize can create alerts on p99>baseline*1.5.

ops-bot: fp-backfill job fp-backfill-20260304 finished window=2026-03-01..2026-03-03 duration=1h32m errors=1 (see #OPS-4821)

izzy: next steps / action items:
- marcos: add partial-index DDL + cluster config for fp_mod (this sprint)
- priya: assemble saved-chart battery and baseline (end of week)
- jong: implement read-planner union pattern in query library (PR target mid-week)
- tom: coordinate backfill windows with SRE and add kill-switch endpoint (tomorrow)
- izzy: write short RFC with cost estimate + sample metrics (today)

marcos: I'll start the DDL PR and include VACUUM strategy notes.

priya: I'll start picking charts and share an automated script to run them against staging.

jong: +1 to review PRs.

izzy: thanks all. ping here if you want to review the RFC. react with :rocket: if you can help on the backfill workers.

marcos: :rocket:
jong: :rocket:
priya: :thumbsup:
